title: traffic-variance-experimentation-notes-and-response-lattice-wip
body:
PURPOSE:
Quick lab notes for a) handling noisy traffic during micro-canaries and b) building a compact signal->action lattice (we call this the Response Lattice) so oncall/launch steward decisions are consistent and fast. This is intentionally informal — sketches, TODOs, and sample queries included.

SCOPE:
- Small to medium surface product launches where sampling slices <= 5% traffic per slice.
- Features sensitive to latency/cost changes (rerankers, multi-model routing, token-heavy generation).
- Works with hybrid inference (hosted + dedicated routing).

KEY IDEA SUMMARY (one-liner):
Curate a prioritized set of orthogonal signals, score them by impact/confidence, and drive a 3-tier lattice of automated gating -> human confirmation -> automatic reversion. The lattice should map signal combos to a single runbook action so stewards don't debate under pressure.

Signal inventory (working):
- Latency P95 and P99 (model-level and route-level): quick proxy for perf regressions.
- Token cost per request (est): spikes indicate model/quantization fallback or new prompt shapes.
- Top-level error rate (5xx/4xx): general health.
- Semantic drift score (eval holdout testset drifter): needs background batch job.
- Sentiment / toxic content fraction (for chat/rerank features).
- Key metric delta: retention/ctr/accept-rate depending on feature.
- Sampling heterogeneity: demographic or cohort imbalance check (to catch sampling bias).

Scoring and weight heuristics (fast, crude):
- Create normalized z-like scores for each signal using short baseline window (last 7 days).
- Weight by product impact multiplier (0.5 low-impact, 1 default, 2 high-impact).
- Confidence factor = 1 / sqrt(sample_size_relative). Lower sample size -> lower confidence.
- Combined risk_score = sum(weighted_signal_score * confidence).

Response Lattice (sketch):
Tier 0 (AUTO): automated mitigation without human action
- Preconditions: risk_score between 0.8 and 1.5 AND pattern matches automated fallback fingerprint (e.g., specific model variant failure).
- Action: route matching traffic to fallback model (pre-registered), throttle burst to 50% traffic, annotate rollout in console.

Tier 1 (HUMAN CONFIRM): open incident window for steward review
- Preconditions: risk_score 1.5 - 3.0 OR cross-signal (latency + semantic drift) where neither is independently catastrophic.
- Action: notify steward channel (pager/Slack), lock cohort expansion, collect synthetic trace pack, run quick diagnostics (queries below).

Tier 2 (ESCALATION & REVERT): human-led rollback or pause
- Preconditions: risk_score > 3.0 OR visible user-facing failure (>= 3% error uplift on exposed endpoints).
- Action: rollback to last known-good model/version, trigger postmortem template, open JIRA with prefilled tags.

Notes on noisy traffic / variance handling:
- Use short-term smoothing windows (3-5m) for latency; use longer windows (1-4h) for business metrics.
- Flag spikes that correlate with external factors: deploys in dependent services, region failures, cloud maintenance. Tag signals with origin if available.
- Synthetic traffic: maintain a small stable synthetic session cohort (0.5% traffic) that exercises core flows and is excluded from user metrics; use as a sanity anchor.

Sample diagnostic queries (Prometheus/BigQuery pseudocode):
- p95_latency_by_model = quantile_over_time(0.95, latency_seconds{route=~"/generate.*",model=~".*"}[5m])
- user_error_rate = sum(errors{env="prod"}) / sum(requests{env="prod"}) by (route)[1h]
- token_cost_delta = (avg(token_cost_per_request)[1h] - avg(token_cost_per_request)[24h]) / avg(token_cost_per_request)[24h]
- semantic_drift = 1 - cosine_similarity(embedding(baseline_prompt_samples), embedding(recent_samples)) (batch job)

Quick checklist for steward when Tier 1 fires:
- Confirm whether synthetic cohort shows same signal? (yes/no)
- Check recent infra deploys in last 30m (link to release pipeline).
- Run 10 targeted queries from Query Pack A (see linked github).
- If evidence of data-driven regression -> hold expansion and notify product PM.
- If evidence of infra flake -> trigger autoscaling/fallback and close window with note.

Rollback matrix (example):
- New model variant: immediate revert to previous variant + block rollout path for 24h if error_rate > 1% absolute uplift.
- Routing rule change: revert routing table and re-check recall metrics on shadow traffic.
- Prompt template change: roll back and run prompt regression harness against curated eval set.

Experimentation/AB considerations specific to LLMs:
- Interference: concurrent A/Bs may influence model cache/localized KV cache behavior. Prefer orthogonal timing or ensure separate runtime pools.
- Exposure decay: signal quality for quality metrics often needs more samples; treat these with longer evaluation windows.
- Cost gating: always track token-unit delta per cohort, abort if cost delta > pre-agreed budget multiplier.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How many synthetic sessions are enough to be a stable anchor? (Priya to run sim to estimate sample variance)
- Define canonical similarity threshold for semantic_drift signal (Samir to propose).
- Integrate response lattice into console view: single-click apply automated fallback? (UX scoping)
- Add region-aware baselines for latency; current baseline is global and hides regional regressions.

Runbook snippets (copyable):
1) When Tier 1 alerts: paste the following into steward Slack thread: "Alert: rollout slice X (5%) elevated risk_score=%. Quick checks: synthetic_cohort=yes/no; infra_deploys=none/ID; p95(latency)=ms; error_rate=%. Next step: hold expansion and collect traces."

2) Auto-fallback policy (yaml sketch):
- name: model-fallback-v1
  trigger: combined_risk_score >= 0.8 and model_variant in [v2-quantized]
  action: route->v1; throttle: 0.5; annotate: "auto-fallback:response-lattice"

Communication & comms templates:
- Short customer note template (if visible): "We detected a performance regression impacting some requests and temporarily routed to an alternative model to preserve responsiveness. We're investigating and will share an update within 2 hours."

Appendix: Observability checklist for experiments
- Per-slice p95/p99 latency by region and model
- Per-slice token consumption and cost estimate
- Per-slice semantic drift and sample size
- Per-slice unique-user ratio (to detect over-sampling)

Raw notes / scribbles:
- Consider adding a quick chart that maps "signal pair states" -> recommended action (table encourages fast decisioning).
- Might be worth a tiny ML classifier that suggests lattice tier but keep human override default.
- Keep the auto-fallback inventory small and audited weekly.
- Edge-case: multi-model cascades where fallback also has regressions -> pre-register second-level fallback or cascade to cached responses.

CONTACTS: Riley Martinez (owner), Priya Desai (signals), Samir Cho (telemetry), Evelyn Brooks (steering), Marta Nguyen (ops).
